newsitem.title: UK: McDonald's to create 5,000 UK jobs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's to create 5,000 UK jobs in 1997.

text.p: McDonalds Restaurants Ltd said on Thursday it planned to open over 100 restaurants in Britain in 1997, creating at least 5,000 new full and part-time jobs in the process.
The expansion represented an investment of more than 116 million pounds in land and buildings, said the fast-food restaurant chain in a statement.

"Nearly 60 percent of restaurant-based management started as hourly-paid staff. A third of McDonald's franchisees, owning and operating their own businesses, are former employees, and half of them started as hourly paid staff. These are real jobs with long term prospects," said McDonald's UK president Andrew Taylor.

McDonalds pays staff an average hourly rate of 3.96 pounds. The company plans to open about 38 more restaurants in the south of England, 27 in the Midlands, 28 in the north, 12 in Scotland and five in Northern Ireland.
In 1996 McDonald's created over 4,500 new jobs and invested 103 million pounds in opening 90 new restaurants.
The company branched out into opening restaurants in more unusual locations during 1996 -- like converted pubs, Stena Ferries, in petrol stations and even inside a Royal Navy base at Devonport.
This trend away from traditional high street and roadside locations is likely to continue.
